plan: Given my private value of $10, my goal is to maximize profit by bidding below my value to ensure a positive gain if I win. Since all values are equally likely, I will bid slightly below my value to avoid overpaying. I will bid $9.9 to maximize the chance of winning while ensuring a gain if I win.

Given my value of $30, I aim to win by bidding just above the likely third-highest bid. With no history, assume bids are uniformly distributed. To maximize profit, bid slightly above half the maximum value, around $25, to outbid lower bids while minimizing payment if winning. This balances the risk of overbidding with the chance of winning and securing a profit.

Given my value of $25, I aim to maximize profit by bidding slightly above the expected average bid. Assuming uniform distribution and no prior history, average value is $24.5. To win, I should bid slightly higher but below my value to ensure profit. I will bid $26 to outbid average values while maintaining a profit margin if I win and pay the third-highest bid. This strategy balances competitiveness and profit potential.
